title: Priority queue & approval SLA for Dedicated onboarding (fair-share + cost smoothing)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As Dedicated demand grows, manual approval queues and single-priority intake are creating long lead times for mid-tier customers while a small set of large customers consume burst windows. This ticket proposes a new prioritized onboarding queue with a fair-share allocator and cost-smoothing rules to reduce approval latency and better utilize provisionable fleet capacity.

Scope: product-level workflow and policy definitions, acceptance criteria for automated priority assignment, audit trails for approvals, and an implementation handoff to Eng for policy enforcement and billing integration. Not included: low-level scheduler/k8s changes (handled by ENG backlog), changes to reserved-contract legal language (handled by Legal).
background: Our current Dedicated provisioning flow processes requests FIFO with manual approvers for >X-GPU reservations. That results in inconsistent approval SLAs and reactive capacity commits. Observations from support logs and sales feedback indicate: (1) 30% of medium-sized intake waits >7 business days, (2) 12% of high-priority requests are delayed during burst windows, and (3) finance billing spikes when multiple customers are granted peak capacity simultaneously.
proposed_workflow: 1) Intake form adds determiners: customer tier, expected qps/throughput, preferred region, commit window, and cost sensitivity. 2) System computes a priority_score = weighted(customer_tier, historical_usage, time_waiting, cost_smoothing_flag). 3) Requests enter a prioritized queue; reviewers see suggested SLA (target approval window) and a recommended allocation plan. 4) Auto-approve rules for low-risk request patterns (small size, existing committed customers). 5) Fair-share allocator reserves burst budget across active pending requests to smooth short-term cost impact. 6) Approval actions generate audit entries and optionally create a provisional Dedicated allocation in sandbox mode for testing. 7) Handoff to provisioning once human or auto-approval completes.
acceptance_criteria: Priority score produced for every incoming request and visible in queue UI
Approval SLA targets defined and met in pilot: P0 requests <= 24h, P1 <= 3 business days, P2 <= 7 business days
Auto-approve rule set implemented for defined patterns with >95% accuracy in pilot
Fair-share budgeting limits prevent >20% billing surge relative to baseline in simulated burst tests
Audit trail records approver, decision, reason, and link to provisioning ticket for every approval
Integration hooks for billing (cost smoothing) and provisioning queues exist and are documented for engineering handoff
decision_log: 2025-08-18: Chosen to prioritize a policy-first approach (PM/Eng/Finance) rather than rewriting provisioning scheduler immediately.
2025-08-22: Agreed weightings for priority_score: customer_tier(40%), historical_usage(25%), time_waiting(20%), cost_smoothing_flag(15%).
2025-08-28: Finance requested a cost-smoothing guardrail: provisional burst budget cannot exceed 10% of month committed spend without manual escalation.
2025-09-01: Design signed off on UI mockups for queue view and decision panel (S. Ramirez).
implementation_notes: Engineering will implement the priority service as a stateless scoring endpoint plus a persisted queue. Billing team will provide an API for provisional budget checks and commit reports. Legal to review auto-approve thresholds for contractual obligations. The feature will be gated behind a feature flag and rollout to internal customers first. Engineering tickets recommended: ENG-6910 (priority-service), ENG-6911 (queue-UI), ENG-6922 (billing-integration).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-scoring could starve high-importance customers. Mitigation: conservative initial weights, human reviewer override, and monitoring for false negatives. Risk: billing spikes if provisional budgets abused. Mitigation: hard guardrails and escalation paths through Finance and Sales Ops.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: feature-flagged to Platform and Sales Eng (2 weeks). 2) Beta: 10 pilot customers across tiers (4 weeks). 3) General availability with telemetry and feature toggles to dial aggressiveness (gradual 8-week ramp).
notes: Prefer to surface intercepts in Console's Dedicated > Intake view; Console team to coordinate UI implementation.
